findings.problem: Explanation for "A hundred measures of barley" says the next debtor owes wheat "so you were just one bill early." Barley is not wheat (Luke 16:7), so the baker's answer would not have been right on the next bill either. What he points out is not true.

rule.text: **Noticing.** What he points out must be true. "Same words" means an exact match.

findings.problem: Explanation for "False" ends "Different numbers, same speedy paperwork." Only the first debtor is told to "sit down quickly" (Luke 16:6). Luke 16:7 says nothing about speed for the second debtor, so "same speedy" adds what the text doesn't say.

rule.text: **Don't stretch the text.** Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Three quotes change the BSB punctuation inside the quotation marks. In "strangers": "the belongings of another." (the BSB has a comma) and "belongings of your own." (the BSB has a question mark). In "rulers": "belongings of your own." (question mark in the BSB). In "family": "belongings of your own." (question mark in the BSB). Luke 16:12 reads "...the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?"

rule.text: **Quotes.** Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks. His own made-up lines in jokes can use quotation marks.

findings.problem: Explanation for "Bigger storehouses" ends "I learned that one the hard way, friend. A bigger drawer just means more room to collect dust." The comparison doesn't match the core action (being trusted with true riches instead of more worldly wealth) and needs explaining to make sense. It also adds a new event to his backstory (learning a lesson about a bigger drawer), which the drawer story in papa-dorin.md doesn't include.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Explanation for "fifty" ends "I have never split a batch that fast, and I've been trying for years." Splitting a batch isn't something that takes years of trying, so the joke doesn't click. The comparison also misses the core action (cutting a debt quickly).

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
